lessons.title: Preparing for a grain inspection
lessons.html:
Why we inspect stored grain

Grain in a silo, bin or bag store is alive in a way. It breathes. If it is too wet or too warm, it starts to heat and go mouldy. Insects like the maize weevil and the flour beetle can grow fast and eat the grain. Rats and birds also come in. Regular inspection finds these problems early, while they are still small.

Get your instructions

Your supervisor will tell you which bins or stacks to inspect, how often, and what to look for. Read the inspection form before you go. It will have spaces for the bin number, date, grain temperature, smell, insects and other notes.

Collect your equipment

  • Inspection form and pen
  • Torch
  • Sampling spear (probe) and sample bags or containers, labelled
  • Sieve and a white tray to look for insects
  • Thermometer or temperature probe, if used on your site
  • Insect trap or probe trap, if used

Put on your PPE

Wear a dust mask, safety boots, gloves and a hard hat where needed. Grain dust can make you sick. If the store has been fumigated, you may not go in until a supervisor confirms it has been cleared as safe. Look for warning signs on the door.

Safety rules

  • Never enter a silo or bin alone. A second person must stand outside and be able to call for help.
  • Never walk on grain while it is being emptied. Moving grain can pull you under in seconds.
  • Do not enter a closed bin unless your supervisor has given permission for confined space entry.
  • Use ladders only if they are in good order and hold on with both hands.

If anything is not safe, stop and tell your supervisor.

lessons.title: Inspecting the grain and the store
lessons.html:
Look at the store first

Walk around the outside and inside of the store. Look for:

  • holes in the roof or walls where rain can come in,
  • wet patches, rust or water marks,
  • rat holes, droppings or chewed bags,
  • bird droppings and feathers,
  • spilled grain around the store,
  • open doors or broken seals.

Use your senses on the grain

CheckGood grainProblem signs
SmellFresh, cleanMusty, sour or mouldy smell
FeelDry, flows easilyDamp, sticky, lumps or crust
TemperatureCool, same all overWarm spot, steam, condensation
LookEven colourMould, webbing, holes in kernels, dust

Take samples

Push the sampling spear into the grain at the places your instruction gives, for example the top, the middle and near the walls. Insects often gather at the top and where it is warm. Put each sample in a labelled bag with the bin number, place and date.

Look for insects

Shake the sample through the sieve onto the white tray. Look closely. Small dark beetles with a long snout are weevils. Small reddish-brown beetles may be flour beetles. Little moths flying above the grain or webbing on the top show grain moths. Count what you find, or follow the method on your form.

Check temperature

If your site uses temperature cables or a probe, read the temperature at the points given. Heating is a warning sign of insects or wet grain. A hot spot must be reported at once.

lessons.title: Completing the inspection
lessons.html:
Write down what you found

Fill in the inspection form while you are at the bin, not later. Write:

  1. Bin or stack number and the date and time.
  2. Grain type, for example white maize, wheat or sunflower.
  3. Temperature readings.
  4. Smell and look of the grain.
  5. Insects found: type and number.
  6. Signs of rats, birds or water damage.
  7. Your name and signature.

Write clearly. Other people will use this form to decide if the grain must be turned, dried, cleaned or fumigated.

Report problems quickly

Tell your supervisor immediately if you find:

  • live insects,
  • a hot spot or steam,
  • wet or mouldy grain,
  • a leaking roof,
  • rats in the store.

Do not try to treat the grain with chemicals yourself. Only trained and registered people may apply fumigants and insecticides.

Hand in samples

Take the labelled samples to the laboratory or grading room as your site requires. Make sure the labels match the form.

Clean up

Close all doors and hatches and check seals. Clean the spear, sieve and tray. Put the equipment back. Throw away used sample bags in the right bin. Wash your hands before you eat or drink.

Key points

  • Inspect stored grain regularly for insects, heating, moisture, rats and birds.
  • Never enter a bin alone or walk on grain that is being emptied.
  • Use smell, feel, temperature and a sieve to check the grain.
  • Fill in the form at the bin and label samples correctly.
  • Report live insects, hot spots and wet grain to your supervisor at once.
